author: giulio-leone
body:
## Issue

Closes #1764

## Description

When using Gemini thinking models (e.g., `gemini-2.5-flash`, `gemini-3-flash`) through the LiteLLM model provider, multi-turn conversations with tool calls fail with:

```
function call 'current_time' in the 2. content block is missing a thought_signature
```

### Root Cause

Gemini thinking models require a `thought_signature` on each function call in multi-turn conversations. LiteLLM encodes this signature into the tool call ID using a `__thought__` separator (e.g., `call_abc__thought__base64sig`). However, Strands' `OpenAIModel.format_chunk()` passes the encoded ID through without extracting the signature into the `reasoningSignature` field that the streaming layer already supports.

While the encoded ID survives the round-trip in simple cases, the signature must also be explicitly stored in `reasoningSignature` so that:
1. The streaming infrastructure can properly track it through content block lifecycle
2. The signature can be re-encoded into the tool call ID even when the ID is cleaned or regenerated
3. `provider_specific_fields.thought_signature` (an alternative LiteLLM transport) is also captured

### Changes

**`src/strands/models/litellm.py`**:
- Override `format_chunk` to detect `__thought__` in tool call IDs and/or `provider_specific_fields.thought_signature`, extracting the signature into `reasoningSignature` on the `contentBlockStart` event
- Override `format_request_message_tool_call` to re-encode `reasoningSignature` back into the tool call ID when not already present, ensuring LiteLLM can reconstruct the Gemini-native format

**`tests/strands/models/test_litellm.py`**:
- 7 new unit tests covering: extraction from encoded ID, extraction from `provider_specific_fields`, no-signature passthrough, signature encoding, double-encode prevention, and full round-trip preservation

## Checklist

- [x] I've read [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] I've updated or added tests to cover changes
- [x] I've verified all existing tests pass (48/48)
- [x] This change is backward compatible (no breaking changes)

author: fivetran-felixhuang
body:
https://docs.snowflake.com/en/sql-reference/functions/strtok

DuckDB doesn't have strtok, so we need to leverage REGEXP_SPLIT_TO_ARRAY to implement Snowflake's behaviors.

There are some special Snowflake behaviors that we need to take care of:

1. In Snowflake, each character in the delimiter string is a separate delimiter. For example, if the delimiter is '@.', then both '@' and '.' are treated as delimiters and they can be matched out of order. We need to wrap the delimiter input with regex group. 
2. Snowflake doesn't return empty strings, we need to filter them out
3. if we have empty delimiter + empty input string , Snowflake returns NULL
4.  If the delimiter is empty, and the input string is non-empty, then the whole string will be treated as one token.
5. Snowflake returns NULL for negative indices
6. Snowflake returns NULL if any argument is NULL

For more details on this please check the comments in strtok_sql

### Testing

Source Snowflake query

```
SELECT
STRTOK('user@snowflake.com', '.@', 2) as a1,
STRTOK('user@snowflake.com', '.@', -1) as a2,
STRTOK('user@snowflake.com', '.@', 0) as a3,
STRTOK('user@snowflake.com', '@.', 8) as a4,
STRTOK('user snowflake com') as a5,
STRTOK('user@snowflake.com', '@.') as a6,
STRTOK('user.snowflake.com') as a7,
STRTOK('user.snowflake.com', '.', 3) as a71,
STRTOK('', '') as a8,
STRTOK('abc', '') as a9,
STRTOK('a', '', 1) as a10,
STRTOK('a', '', 2) as a101,
STRTOK('a', '', -1) as a102,
STRTOK('.b.', '.', 1) as a11,
STRTOK('.b.c.d.', '.', 2) as a12,
STRTOK('..', '.', 1) as a122,
STRTOK(NULL, '@.', 2) as a13,
STRTOK('a.b.c$g', NULL, 2) as a14,
STRTOK('a b c', ' ', 2) as a16,
STRTOK('user@snowflake.com', SUBSTR('.@^', 1, 2), 2) as a17,
STRTOK('ab', IFNULL(NULL, '')) as a18,
STRTOK('ab', IFNULL(NULL, ''), 1) as a19,
STRTOK('ab', IFNULL(NULL, ''), 2) as a20,
STRTOK('ab', IFNULL(NULL, ''), 0) as a21,
STRTOK('a.b.c', ifnull('.', '.'), 2) as b2,
 STRTOK('a[b]c', ifnull('[]', '[]'), 2) as b3,
 STRTOK('a^b^c', ifnull('^', '^'), 2) as b4,
 STRTOK('a-b-c', ifnull('-', '-'), 2) as b5,
 STRTOK('abc', ifnull('', ''), 2) as b6,
 STRTOK('a+b+c', ifnull('+', '+'), 2) as b7,
 STRTOK('a?b?c', ifnull('?', '?'), 2) as b8,
 STRTOK('a(b)c', ifnull('()', '()'), 2) as b9,
 STRTOK('a{b}c', ifnull('{}', '{}'), 2) as b10,
 STRTOK('a|b|c', ifnull('|', '|'), 2) as b11,
 STRTOK('a$b$c', ifnull('$', '$'), 2) as b12,
 STRTOK('user@snowflake.com', SUBSTR('.@^', 1, 2), 2) as b13,
 STRTOK('a./b/cg', ifnull('/.', '/.'), 3) as b14,

STRTOK('a$b/cg', '$/.', NULLIFZERO(1-1)) as c1,
STRTOK('a$b/cg', '$/.', 1) as c2,
STRTOK('a$b/c*g', '$/.', 2) as c3,

-- problematic
STRTOK('a.b\cg', ifnull('\.', '\.'), 3) as d1,
STRTOK('a.b\cg', '\.', NULLIFZERO(1-1)) as d2,
STRTOK('a.b\cg', '\.', 1) as d3,
STRTOK('a.b\cg', '\\', 1) as d4,
STRTOK('a.b\cg', '\.', 3) as d5,
STRTOK('a.b\cg', '\.', 4) as d6,
STRTOK('a.b\cg', '.', 2) as d7,
STRTOK('a.b\cg', '*', 2) as d8,
```

The transpiled query works except for the problematic statements that contain the escape character '\' in the input or delimiter

author: jaybosamiya-ms
body:
This PR fully eliminates the descriptor table indirection we had in the shim, now relying entirely on the LiteBox core to manage file descriptors both for raw FDs as well as the typed FDs.

To do this, I've made the following changes at the core litebox crate:
* Explicitly started allowing for non-`litebox` crates to define `FdEnabledSubsystem`s, as a stabilized interface
* Exposed some public interfaces to interact more with the descriptor tables
* Introduced a `EntryHandle` interface, that allows entry-specific locking _outside_ `litebox` without maintaining a full descriptor table lock

At the shim, roughly it boils down to "remove `Descriptors` + `Descriptor`" and deal with the consequences.  The changes are quite extensive but are not particularly insightful in any major way.  I did clean up a few bugs along the way where (say) rlimits might not have been adhered to, or if two descriptors are made and the second one hit an rlimit issue, then there could have been a leak, etc.

Despite removing a chunk of code, some other code _did_ get a tiny bit more bloated, but the level of indirection is smaller.  I think we can further clean this up by removing some of the redundancy, but I think merging this in sooner than that is probably the better move, thus I've opened the PR in the current state.

---

author: masonc15
body:
## Problem

`spogo library tracks list` could return an empty success from the Connect client.

The previous implementation queried `libraryV3` with the `Songs` filter. In current Spotify responses, that request behaves like an invalid liked-songs path: the payload can include `LibraryInvalidFilterIdError` while still decoding to zero items, so the web API fallback never activates.

Liked songs are available through `fetchLibraryTracks` for `spotify:collection:tracks`, but that operation returns a different shape: `data.me.library.tracks.items[].track.data`, with `_uri` on the `track` wrapper rather than inside `data`.

## Changes

- Switch `libraryTracks()` from `libraryV3` to `fetchLibraryTracks` with `spotify:collection:tracks`.
- Add a dedicated extractor for the `fetchLibraryTracks` payload and inject `_uri` into the extracted track data before mapping.
- Treat missing or malformed `fetchLibraryTracks` payloads as errors so `LibraryTracks()` falls back to the web API instead of silently returning an empty result.
- Tighten tests to validate the `fetchLibraryTracks` request variables and cover the fallback path when the response shape drifts.

## Testing

- `go test ./...`
- Manually verified `spogo library tracks list --limit 5`
- Manually verified `spogo library tracks list --limit 3 --json`

### Motivation

- Simplify the search UI by removing the exact/contains radio controls and avoid maintaining extra widget state.
- Make search behavior consistent and less error-prone by always using a case-insensitive substring match instead of a word-boundary regex exact mode. 

### Description

- Removed the `contains`/`exact` `QRadioButton`s and the `QButtonGroup` from the search panel in `ManageChartsDialog` and eliminated their layout. 
- Stopped touching the removed `search_text_contains` control in `_clear_filters`. 
- Replaced the regex-based `search_exact` branch in `_chart_matches_filters` with a single case-insensitive substring check implemented in `matches(...)`. 
- Kept all other filter behavior unchanged while simplifying search-related state and logic. 

### Testing

- Ran the project's automated test suite with `pytest` against the modified code and all tests passed.

body:
### Motivation
- Frontend history UIs expect a flattened/recent-oriented payload but the backend returned only legacy `{"category::intent": bucket}` maps, causing history to appear missing in the UI.
- The fix preserves existing categorized storage while exposing a stable, frontend-friendly shape and a dedicated recent endpoint for the terminal right-panel.
- Storage backend detection remains PostgreSQL → Object Storage → Replit DB → local JSON, and in this runtime PostgreSQL/Object Storage are not available so the code falls back to local JSON files (i.e. no durable DB configured).

### Description
- Added `_shape_prompt_history(all_history, recent_limit=10)` in `main.py` to produce a payload containing `buckets`, `categories`, `items`, `recent`, and counts while preserving original bucket grouping.
- Updated `GET /api/history` to return the shaped payload by default, accept `recent_limit` query param, and keep backward compatibility via `?format=legacy|raw` which returns the original bucket map.
- Added `GET /api/history/recent?limit=10` to return only the recent N flattened items and counts for quick consumption by the terminal/right-history panel.
- Only `main.py` was modified; prompt/chat write paths and storage selection in `data/prompt_history.py` and `data/chat_history.py` were left intact to preserve existing persistence logic and preset formatting.

- Ran `python -m py_compile main.py data/chat_history.py data/prompt_history.py data/pg_storage.py` which succeeded with no syntax errors.
- Executed a runtime detection script that printed history backend diagnostics and confirmed `_use_postgres` and `_use_object_storage` are `False` and the runtime is using the local JSON fallback (no durable DB available).

author: copilot
body:
`backend-go/cmd/server/main.go` had duplicate/overlapping code blocks from a bad merge, causing compilation failure and a Render deploy crash where MongoDB URIs were fed to the PostgreSQL driver.

## Backend fix (`backend-go/cmd/server/main.go`)

- Removed orphaned `database.NewDatabase()` call (PostgreSQL-only) that bypassed the URI-scheme factory and left an unclosed `if err != nil {` block swallowing startup logs
- Replaced with `database.NewDatabaseFromURL()` inside the existing retry loop, typed against the `database.DB` interface — handles both PostgreSQL DSNs and `mongodb://`/`mongodb+srv://` URIs
- Removed duplicate `app.Listen("0.0.0.0:" + port)` line in the server goroutine

```go
// Before: bypassed factory, crashed on MongoDB URIs
var db *database.Database
db, err = database.NewDatabase(dbURL)  // PostgreSQL driver only

// After: auto-detects scheme, retries on slow DB start
var db database.DB
db, err = database.NewDatabaseFromURL(dbURL)  // routes mongodb:// to Mongo driver
```

This is the root cause of the deploy error:
```
missing "=" after "******mongodb.railway.internal:27017" in connection info string
```

author: velisiska
body:
## Summary

- Problem: When a qmd document path is slugified (e.g. by the qmd index), the file doesn't exist at the expected filesystem location and `readFile` returns empty text
- Why it matters: Agents reading memory docs get blank content for valid qmd documents with slugified paths
- What changed: Added a `qmd get` fallback in `readFile` — when a `qmd/` file is missing on disk, it converts the path to a `qmd://` URI and delegates to `qmd get` which can resolve slugified paths. Extracted `getQmdFile` as a clean helper that accepts a ready URI
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): Path-traversal protections (`resolveReadPath` collection allow-list + `isWithinRoot`) still run before the fallback; no changes to write paths or search

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Memory / storage

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related: n/a

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Memory `readFile` now returns document content for slugified qmd paths instead of empty text.

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- New/changed network calls? No
- Command/tool execution surface changed? No — `qmd get` is already available; this adds a new call site bounded by existing collection allow-list and `isWithinRoot` checks
- Data access scope changed? No

## Repro + Verification

### Steps

1. Create a qmd collection with a document that gets a slugified path
2. Call `readFile` with the slugified `qmd/<collection>/<slug>.md` path
3. Before fix: returns `{ text: "" }`; after fix: returns the document content

### Expected

- Document content returned via `qmd get` fallback

### Actual (before fix)

- Empty text returned

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- 3 new tests: happy-path fallback, `from`/`lines` slicing, `qmd get` failure gracefully returns empty text

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: all 3 new tests pass (`pnpm test -- src/memory/qmd-manager.test.ts`)
- Edge cases checked: `qmd get` failure returns empty text (not error); `from`/`lines` slicing works on fallback content
- What you did **not** verify: end-to-end with a real `qmd` binary (mocked in tests)

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config/env changes? No
- Migration needed? No

## Failure Recovery (if this breaks)

- How to disable/revert this change quickly: revert the commit on `src/memory/qmd-manager.ts`
- Known bad symptoms reviewers should watch for: unexpected `qmd get` spawns for non-slugified paths (should not happen — fallback only triggers when file is missing on disk)

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: Extra `qmd get` spawn for genuinely missing files (not slugified, just nonexistent)
  - Mitigation: `getQmdFile` returns `null` on failure; falls through to existing empty-text return. Cost is one bounded subprocess call with the configured timeout.

### Universal Prediction Engine (UPE)
- **7 prediction slices** with response_type filtering to prevent cross-type contamination in CBR lookups

- **LanceDB `response_type` field** added to embeddings schema, `add_decision()`, and `find_similar()`

author: csiege
body:
## Summary

Adds **HV-Lint**, an on-demand GitHub Actions workflow that validates HV transformation YAML files for structural correctness (Phase 1) and dbGaP cross-reference accuracy (Phase 2).

Resolves #392.

---

## What's included

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `hv-lint/validate_yaml_quality.py` | Phase 1: Schema-driven structural checks (1.1–1.10) |
| `hv-lint/validate_phv_cross_reference.py` | Phase 2: dbGaP PHV/PHT cross-reference validation (2.1–2.5) |
| `hv-lint/build_phv_index.py` | Builds compressed PHV→PHT indexes from raw dbGaP HTML cache |
| `hv-lint/dbgap-cache/*.json.gz` | Pre-built compressed indexes for all 10 cohorts (~425 KB total) |
| `.github/workflows/hv_lint.yml` | GitHub Actions workflow definition |

## Workflow: on-demand only

This workflow is **`workflow_dispatch` only** — it does not trigger on push, PR, or any other event. It must be run manually from the Actions tab or via `gh workflow run`.

### How to run

**From the GitHub UI:**
1. Go to **Actions → HV-Lint Quality Checks**
2. Click **Run workflow**
3. Select the branch (e.g., `feature/392-hv-lint` or `main` after merge)
4. Configure the inputs (see below)
5. Click **Run workflow**

**From the CLI:**
```bash
gh workflow run hv_lint.yml --ref main \
  -f cohort=chs -f bdchm_ref=main -f fail_on=error -f summary_limit=100
```

### Workflow inputs

| Input | Default | Description |
|-------|---------|-------------|
| **Use workflow from** | (branch selector) | Which branch to check out — must contain the `hv-lint/` scripts |
| **BDCHM schema git ref** | `main` | Git ref (branch/tag/SHA) for the BDCHM schema used in Phase 1 slot validation |
| **Cohort to validate** | `all` | Single cohort name (e.g., `CHS`, `ARIC`) or `all` for every cohort |
| **Minimum severity to fail** | `error` | Lowest severity that causes a non-zero exit: `critical`, `error`, `warning`, or `info` |
| **Max findings in summary** | `50` | Number of findings shown in the Markdown step summary on the run page. Increase for more detail; full results are always in the raw log. |

### Output

- **Step Summary**: A formatted Markdown table rendered directly on the workflow run page (not subject to GitHub's 10-annotation-per-severity limit)
- **Artifact**: Summary files are uploaded as a downloadable `hv-lint-findings` artifact
- **Annotations**: Findings are also emitted as GitHub annotations (limited to 10 per severity by GitHub)
- **Raw logs**: Full untruncated output is always available in the step logs

## Test results (CHS, 2026-03-12)

| Phase | Files | Blocks | Findings |
|-------|-------|--------|----------|
| Phase 1 | 142 | 1,323 | 500 ERROR, 362 HIGH |
| Phase 2 | 142 | 1,323 | 2 WARNING, 18 INFO |

The majority of Phase 1 ERRORs are the known `expsoure_provenance` typo (should be `exposure_provenance`) across DrugExposure blocks — a pre-existing data issue, not a linter bug.

## What's NOT included (future work)

- Checks 1.8, 1.11, 2.4, 2.6–2.9 (see #392 for full list)
- Phase 3: Regression detection
- Automatic triggers (push/PR) — intentionally deferred until findings are triaged

body:
## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code action repo](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action).

After merging this PR, let's try mentioning @claude in a comment on any PR to get started!

author: wallyben
body:
## Summary

This PR upgrades the Pokemon Stencil Art Factory from a DreamShaper SD 1.5-based pipeline to a modern SDXL + IP-Adapter + ControlNet stack. The new architecture provides significantly higher quality image generation at 1024×1024 resolution with improved character preservation through reference image encoding.

## Key Changes

### Core Pipeline Architecture
- **Base Model**: Upgraded from DreamShaper (SD 1.5) to `stabilityai/stable-diffusion-xl-base-1.0`
- **Pipeline**: Replaced `StableDiffusionControlNetPipeline` with `StableDiffusionXLControlNetPipeline`
- **ControlNets**: Updated to SDXL-compatible variants:
  - OpenPose: `thibaud/controlnet-openpose-sdxl-1.0`
  - Canny: `diffusers/controlnet-canny-sdxl-1.0`
- **New Feature**: IP-Adapter conditioning (`h94/IP-Adapter`) for reference image encoding with 0.45 scale factor
- **Generation Settings**: 28 inference steps, guidance_scale=7.5, 1024×1024 output

### Model Loading & Caching (`model_loader.py`)
- Added `load_sdxl_controlnet_pipeline()` as the primary loader function
- Introduced separate `_SDXL_CACHE` for SDXL pipeline instances
- IP-Adapter weights are loaded and configured after pipeline initialization
- Legacy SD 1.5 loaders retained for backward compatibility
- Cache keys now include IP-Adapter and LoRA configuration

### Configuration (`config.py`)
- New SDXL model constants: `DEFAULT_SDXL_LOCAL_PATH`, `DEFAULT_SDXL_HUB_ID`
- New IP-Adapter configuration fields:
  - `use_ip_adapter` (default True)
  - `ip_adapter_scale` (0.45)
  - `ip_adapter_min_images` / `ip_adapter_max_images` (10–30)
- Added `lora_dir` field and `DEFAULT_LORA_DIR` constant
- Legacy model paths renamed with `legacy_` prefix for clarity
- Updated docstrings to reflect v3 architecture

### Image Generation (`generator.py`)
- Refactored `_generate_one()` to dispatch exclusively to SDXL pipeline
- Removed legacy SD 1.5 generation path
- Added `pose_reference` parameter for explicit pose guidance
- Implemented `_load_reference_images()` to load 10–30 reference images from `refs/<pokemon_name>/`
- IP-Adapter conditioning applied via `set_ip_adapter_scale()` when enabled
- Improved prompt template with stencil-friendly composition guidance
- Enhanced logging to track IP-Adapter and ControlNet usage

### Dashboard UI (`app.py`)
- Updated model selection dropdown to prioritize SDXL (recommended)
- Added IP-Adapter toggle control
- Added LoRA model selection dropdown with `_get_available_loras()` helper
- Adjusted generation parameters based on selected model (SDXL: 28 steps/1024×1024, legacy: 20 steps/768×768)
- Updated sidebar branding to "v3 — SDXL + IP-Adapter + ControlNet"
- Added candidate preview grid display

### Model Manager (`model_manager.py`)
- Updated registry to include SDXL base model and IP-Adapter
- Added `lora_names()` method to enumerate available LoRA files
- Added `ensure_directories()` to create lora/ subdirectory
- Added integrity verification for IP-Adapter required files
- Updated logging and status reporting for new models

### Image Processing
- **Segmenter**: Added optional adjacent region merging to reduce layer count to 4–8 for stencil painting
- **Simplifier**: Added colour noise reduction stage before median blur

### Factory Runner (`factory_runner.py`)
- Updated config serialization to include IP-Adapter and legacy model paths

author: tuanknguyen
body:
## Notes to Reviewers

This PR replaces the **watchdog-based polling architecture** with an **event-driven pub/sub system** for terminal output processing, status detection, and inbox message delivery. Terminal output now streams through named FIFOs into an in-process event bus, eliminating filesystem polling and expensive tmux subprocess calls.


| Category | Files | Review Priority |
|----------|-------|----------------|
| **Event bus core** | `event_bus.py`, `fifo_reader.py`, `status_monitor.py`, `log_writer.py` | **Critical** — new infrastructure, threading/async boundary |
| **Async conversion** | `base.py`, all 5 providers, `terminal.py` (utils) | **High** — `time.sleep` → `await asyncio.sleep` throughout init chain |
| **Service rewrites** | `inbox_service.py`, `terminal_service.py`, `main.py` (lifespan) | **High** — wiring changes, startup/shutdown lifecycle |
| **Cleanup paths** | `session_service.py`, `cleanup_service.py`, `terminal_service.delete_terminal` | **Medium** — FIFO + state cleanup on delete |
| **Docs & config** | `event-driven-architecture.md`, `CODEBASE.md`, `constants.py`, `pyproject.toml` | Low |
| **Tests** | `test_codex_provider_unit.py`, `test_gemini_cli_unit.py`, `test_inbox_service.py` | Low — adapted to new signatures |

**Start here:** Read [`docs/event-driven-architecture.md`](event-driven-architecture.md) for the full architecture overview, ASCII data-flow diagram, and component roles before diving into code.

**Key changes:**
- Introduced an in-process **EventBus** with wildcard topic matching and thread-safe publishing
- Replaced watchdog `PollingObserver` with **FIFO readers** (named pipes + `os.read()`) for real-time terminal output streaming
- Added **StatusMonitor** (rolling 8KB buffer + provider pattern matching) as the single source of truth for terminal status
- Added **LogWriter** consumer for debug log persistence
- Refactored **InboxService** from file-watching handler to event-driven consumer
- Converted the entire initialization chain to **async** (`initialize()`, `wait_for_shell()`, `wait_until_status()`)
- Removed `watchdog` and `aiofiles` dependencies

body:
# Overview

### What is the feature?

We need to update dependencies for EDSC on `snyk` findings

### What is the Solution?

Updates dependencies using the `npm audit fix` CLI
When updating the `@aws-sdk`, `client-sqs` tool serialization has become more strict as a result a change needed to be made to update a test. Additionally, for local development we use `elastic-mq` which failed to recieve messages for creating retrievals when in use (e.g. when running start-optionals) this turned out to be because the `orderDelay` was being parsed as undefined. Prior versions where able to accomodate for this but, this newer version resulted in errors propogating from elasticmq. The errors can be resolved simply by assigning a value to `ORDER_DELAY_SECONDS` in `bashrc` but, this adds some robustness. In production this would not occur which was seen in testing, as the value is defaulted and set by the `cdk` deployment

I did also try simply pulling the latest `elasticmq` version `[1.6.16]`(https://hub.docker.com/layers/softwaremill/elasticmq/1.6.16/images/sha256-ef07956a1f734e8ce7d0db5cd63d87b3f0ae3d37ae404c60237bf382f0f4f2cb) that this time but, that didn't make a difference

This change occurred between `
3.913.0 << 3.955.0` these versions. Since the `https://github.com/aws/aws-sdk-js-v3` does rolling updates there are many possible versions where this would have broken.

### What areas of the application does this impact?

Application dependencies creating retrievals and their default delay value 

# Testing

### Reproduction steps

- **Environment for testing:*SIT*
- **Collection to test with:*Any (with customizations)*

1. Start EDSC local with elastic-mq turned on (You may need to pull it from docker-hub) using `npm run start:optionals`
2. Regression test behavior involving the SQS queue: make a Harmony request or echo-orders.
3. Use the requeue feature on the admin portal
4. Ensure the `snyk` issues are resolved

author: lwaldron
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes three bugs in the bioc-run script that could cause issues on case-sensitive filesystems, create duplicate configuration entries, and potentially fail to match GitHub tokens.

## Bugs Fixed

### 1. Path Case Inconsistency (Critical on Linux)

**Issue:** Volume mount paths used inconsistent capitalization - lowercase `r` in some places, uppercase `R` in others.

**Affected Lines:** 165, 170, 189, 192

**Impact:** On case-sensitive filesystems (Linux), the ownership reset operations (`-r` flag) and permission fixes would operate on different paths than the actual runtime mounts, causing permission issues or silently failing.

**Example:**
```bash
# Before fix (on Linux with case-sensitive filesystem):
# Reset ownership tries to fix: /usr/local/lib/r/host-site-library
# But R actually uses:         /usr/local/lib/R/host-site-library
# Result: Permission fixes do not apply to the correct directory
```

**Fix:** Changed all instances to use uppercase `R` for consistency:
```diff
-        -v $DOCKER_RPKGS:/usr/local/lib/r/host-site-library \
+        -v $DOCKER_RPKGS:/usr/local/lib/R/host-site-library \
```

---

### 2. Variable Name Typo

**Issue:** Line 142 checked undefined variable `HLIBENV` instead of `HLIBUSER` (defined on line 141).

**Impact:** The condition always evaluated to true (empty variable), causing `R_LIBS_USER` to be appended to `.Renviron` on every run, even if it already existed.

**Example:**
```bash
# After running bioc-run multiple times, .Renviron would contain:
R_LIBS_USER=/usr/local/lib/R/host-site-library
R_LIBS_USER=/usr/local/lib/R/host-site-library
R_LIBS_USER=/usr/local/lib/R/host-site-library
# ... duplicated on each run
```

**Fix:** Corrected variable name:
```diff
 HLIBUSER=$(grep "R_LIBS_USER" ~/.Renviron)
-if [ -z "${HLIBENV// }" ]; then
+if [ -z "${HLIBUSER// }" ]; then
```

---

### 3. Regex Pattern Bug

**Issue:** Pattern `GITHUB_[P|T].*` incorrectly used pipe `|` inside character class brackets.

**Impact:** In regex character classes `[...]`, the pipe is treated as a literal character, not alternation. This pattern matches `GITHUB_P`, `GITHUB_T`, or `GITHUB_|` followed by anything - potentially missing valid tokens or matching unexpected patterns.

**Example:**
```bash
# Pattern GITHUB_[P|T].* matches:
GITHUB_PAT=...     # ✓ Works (matches P)
GITHUB_TOKEN=...   # ✓ Works (matches T)
GITHUB_|ANYTHING=  # ✗ Also matches (treats | as literal)

# Correct pattern GITHUB_[PT].* matches:
GITHUB_PAT=...     # ✓ Works (matches P)
GITHUB_TOKEN=...   # ✓ Works (matches T)
GITHUB_|ANYTHING=  # ✗ No match (correct behavior)
```

**Fix:** Removed unnecessary pipe from character class:
```diff
-TOKEN_EXP='GITHUB_[P|T].*'
+TOKEN_EXP='GITHUB_[PT].*'
```

## Testing

Tested on macOS. Linux users should verify the ownership reset functionality works correctly with the case-sensitivity fix.

author: alex-solovyev
body:
## Summary

Fixes GH#4294 — `read:file_not_found` pattern observed 376x across 11 models in session-miner feedback loop.

### Root causes identified

1. **`extract.py` line 897**: `args.db.stat().st_size` was called before `connect_db()`, which has the existence check. If the DB path doesn't exist, Python raises an unhandled `FileNotFoundError` before the helpful error message fires.

2. **`compress.py` module-level code**: `CHUNKS_DIR` was used without checking if it exists. If extraction failed or produced no chunks dir, compress.py would fail with a confusing `FileNotFoundError` deep in glob calls.

3. **`compress.py` `main()`**: `OUTPUT.write_text()` assumed the parent directory exists. On a fresh install or after a workspace wipe, the parent dir may not exist yet.

4. **`session-miner-pulse.sh`**: After `run_compression` succeeded (exit 0), the script assumed `compressed_signals.json` was produced. If compression ran but produced no output (e.g., empty chunks), downstream `generate_summary` and `generate_feedback_actions` would fail with "Compressed signals file not found".

### Changes

- **`extract.py`**: Add explicit `args.db.exists()` check before `stat()` call, with a clear error message and `sys.exit(1)`.
- **`compress.py`**: Add `CHUNKS_DIR.exists()` check at module level (before any processing); add `OUTPUT.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` before `write_text()`.
- **`session-miner-pulse.sh`**: Add `[[ -f "${compressed_file}" ]]` guard after compression, before passing the path to `generate_summary` and `generate_feedback_actions`.
- **`prompts/build.txt`**: Update `read:file_not_found` frequency (53x → 376x), document the script-level fix, and add a new rule: *"Before reading any file produced by a prior step, verify it exists — do not assume a successful prior step always produces output."*

### Verification

Re-run session-miner pulse and compare `read:file_not_found` frequency against the 376x baseline. The script-level fixes eliminate the cases where the miner itself was the source of these errors.

Closes #4294

author: process-failed-successfully
body:
**What**: Hoisted `regexp.MustCompile` out of function scopes in several `cmd/recac` files to global scope.
**Why**: Compiling a regular expression is a relatively expensive operation because it parses the pattern and constructs a state machine. Compiling it inside a function means it gets re-compiled every single time the function is called.
**Impact**: Eliminates unnecessary recompilation of regular expressions in various CLI commands, avoiding potentially measurable bottlenecks if these commands are called frequently (especially in CI or scripting loops).
**Measurement**: You can observe the improvement using Go's pprof tools before and after the change on loops invoking these functions, particularly the `regexp.MustCompile` overhead which should disappear from the hot path.

CASS Memory is a TypeScript/Bun MCP server with three-layer architecture: episodic (raw session logs), working (structured summaries), procedural (confidence-tracked rules). Steps: (1) Feed foreman run logs into CASS episodic layer, (2) Run reflection after pipeline completion to update working/procedural memory, (3) Inject relevant memories via 'cm context <task> --json' into TASK.md before agent dispatch, (4) Parse agent feedback comments for memory reinforcement. Replaces foreman-7e84 (build our own memory). Depends on having enough session history.

body:
# Overview 
This PR adds the required workflows and query updates needed to be added as a tree-sitter grammar in the `nvimtreesitter` repo. 

## Key Changes 

- Added/updated CI and release automation workflows.
- Added npm and PyPI publishing jobs.
- Split Rust publishing into two crates:
  - `tree-sitter-objectscript` (UDL grammar)
  - `tree-sitter-objectscript-playground` (playground grammar)
- Added ObjectScript `PRINT`/`ZPRINT` parsing support and corpus tests.
- Refined bindings coverage and packaging layout (Node, Python, Go, Rust).
- Added query sync automation (`scripts/sync_queries.py`) and git pre-commit hook.

## Workflow Changes (Detailed)

### `.github/workflows/ci.yml`

- Triggered on `push`, `pull_request` (branch `main`), and `workflow_dispatch`.
- Adds `concurrency` cancellation for in-progress duplicate runs.
- `test` job:
  - Matrix OS: Ubuntu/Windows/macOS.
  - Uses `tree-sitter/parser-test-action@v3`.
  - Tests parser + Rust + Node + Python + Go + Swift.
  - Runs parser tests for all 4 grammar directories (`objectscript`, `udl`, `core`, `expr`).
- `query` job:
  - Installs `ts_query_ls`.
  - Runs `make checkquery`.
- `examples` job:
  - Parses all `examples/*.cls` files with UDL parser.

### `.github/workflows/lint.yml`

- Triggered on `push`, `pull_request` (branch `main`), and `workflow_dispatch`.
- `lint_js` job:
  - Uses Node 22.
  - Uses `npm ci --legacy-peer-deps --ignore-scripts`.
  - Runs ESLint (`npm run lint`).
- `lint_queries` job:
  - Uses `ts_query_ls`.
  - Runs `make formatquery` and fails if formatting changed query files.
  - Runs `make lintquery`.

### `.github/workflows/fuzz.yml`

- Triggered on `push`, `pull_request` (branch `main`), and `workflow_dispatch`.
- Runs scanner fuzzing via `tree-sitter/fuzz-action@v4`.
- Matrix over `objectscript`, `udl`, `core`.
- Includes guard to skip template/initial-commit scenarios.
- Fuzz run is conditional on scanner changes (`common/scanner.h`) or missing parent commit.

### `.github/workflows/sync-queries.yml`

- Triggered on `push`, `pull_request` (branch `main`), and `workflow_dispatch`.
- Verifies Python query directories stay synced with source query directories.
- Executes:
  - `python3 scripts/sync_queries.py --check-python`

### `.github/workflows/publish.yml`

- Triggered on tag push (`on.push.tags: ["*"]`).
- Permissions include `contents`, `id-token`, and `attestations`.
- Every publish job is guarded with `if: github.repository == 'intersystems/tree-sitter-objectscript'`.
- Jobs:
  - `github`: reusable `tree-sitter/workflows` release workflow (`generate: true`).
  - `npm`: reusable npm package workflow with `NPM_TOKEN`.
  - `pypi`: reusable PyPI package workflow with `PYPI_API_TOKEN`.
  - `crates`: reusable crates.io workflow with `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`.
  - `crates_playground`: custom publish job for `tree-sitter-objectscript-playground`, using `scripts/rust_playground_crate.sh publish`.

## Publishing and Package Distribution

### Package Links

- npm: [tree-sitter-objectscript](https://www.npmjs.com/package/tree-sitter-objectscript)
- PyPI: [tree-sitter-objectscript](https://pypi.org/project/tree-sitter-objectscript/)
- crates.io (UDL): [tree-sitter-objectscript](https://crates.io/crates/tree-sitter-objectscript)
- crates.io (playground): [tree-sitter-objectscript-playground](https://crates.io/crates/tree-sitter-objectscript-playground)

### npm

- Package metadata/versioning updated for release (`1.5.1`).
- `package.json` `files` expanded to include `core` and `expr` grammar/query/source assets, in addition to `objectscript` and `udl`.
- Node engine constraints documented via `.nvmrc` (Node 22) and `engines`.

### PyPI

- `pyproject.toml` updated:
  - Version `1.5.1`
  - `requires-python` bumped to `>=3.9`
  - cibuildwheel selector changed from `cp38-*` to `cp39-*`
- Python packaging narrowed to primary grammar packages:
  - `tree_sitter_objectscript`
  - `tree_sitter_objectscript_udl`
- Query distribution now managed through sync script + checks.

### crates.io (Rust)

- Root crate `tree-sitter-objectscript` now targets UDL grammar only.
- New crate template added: `bindings/rust-playground/` for `tree-sitter-objectscript-playground`.
- Added `scripts/rust_playground_crate.sh` to stage/package/publish playground crate from canonical sources without committing duplicate payload.
- Updated crate readmes:
  - `cargo_readme.md` (UDL crate)
  - `cargo_readme_playground.md` (playground crate)

## Binding Changes

### Node bindings

- Removed `objectscript_core` and `objectscript_expr` exports from Node native binding and TypeScript declarations.
- Node package now exposes:
  - `objectscript`
  - `objectscript_udl`
- Updated tests accordingly.
- `binding.gyp` trimmed to compile only objectscript + UDL C sources.

### Python bindings

- Tests reduced to `objectscript` and `objectscript_udl` modules.
- Packaging (`setup.py`) adjusted to include only these two Python packages and their query files.
- Added query synchronization tooling:
  - `scripts/sync_queries.py`
  - `.githooks/pre-commit` auto-runs sync and stages generated query updates.
- Added workflow enforcement (`sync-queries.yml`) to prevent divergence.

### Go bindings

- Reorganized Go binding files into top-level `bindings/go/*.go`.
- Added a consolidated `bindings/go/binding_test.go`.
- Maintains loadable language accessors for:
  - `objectscript`
  - `objectscript_udl`
  - `objectscript_core`
  - `objectscript_expr`

### Rust bindings

- `bindings/rust` now compiles only UDL parser/scanner and exposes UDL query/node-type constants.
- Added separate `bindings/rust-playground` crate target for playground grammar.
- Publish automation supports both Rust crates.

## Grammar Feature: `PRINT` and `ZPRINT`

### Added language support

- Added new statement rule in `core/grammar.js`:
  - `print_statement`
  - `print_argument`
- Added keywords:
  - `keyword_print` (`P`/`PRINT`)
  - `keyword_zprint` (`ZP`/`ZPRINT`)
- Supports:
  - argumentless forms (`PRINT`, `ZPRINT`, abbreviations)
  - postconditionals (`PRINT:pc`)
  - line references and ranges (`label^routine:label^routine`)
  - indirection in line references

### Added tests
Added tests for the print/zprint statements

## Query lint/ changes 

- Add `.tsqueryrc.json`, which is used in the lint workflow to verify the queries are valid according to `nvimtreesitter` standards
- Added `scripts/sync_queries.py` for layered query composition and Python query copying. Now, for example, udl highlights.scm file contains all the highlights it needs (expr + core + udl). 
- Make targets added/updated for query format/lint/check (`formatquery`, `lintquery`, `checkquery`, `query`).
- Added hook installer target and repository hook path configuration (`make installhooks`).

## Documentation 

- Added `CONTRIBUTING.md`.
- Refactored `README.md` into concise overview + links to contributing instructions.
- Added issue templates under `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/`.

author: devinrosen
body:
## Summary

The [tinted-theming/base16-schemes](https://github.com/tinted-theming/base16-schemes) library and virtually all community base16 theme files use the classic flat format — top-level `base0X` keys with a `scheme:` name field. The YAML parser was written expecting a nested `palette:` section, causing every file from that library to fail silently during discovery.

**Old format (what everyone actually has):**
```yaml
scheme: "Black Metal"
base00: "000000"
base08: "5f8787"
# ...
```

**New nested format (what the parser expected):**
```yaml
name: "Black Metal"
palette:
  base00: "000000"
  base08: "5f8787"
```

## Fix

- `from_base16_yaml_file`: detect format by presence of top-level `base08`; parse flat keys directly, fall back to `palette:` for forward compatibility
- `yaml_display_name`: try `scheme:` first, then `name:`, then filename stem

## Test plan

author: copilot
body:
Two recurring failures when running long bash commands (e.g. `git clone`) through the pi runner:

1. **"Model tried to call unavailable tool 'bash'. No tools are available."** – `SessionManager.continueRecent()` was loading stale session history from previous runs in persistent containers, polluting the fresh conversation context and causing the LLM API to reject tool calls.

2. **Tool timeout displays raw JSON instead of readable text** – pi's internal `ToolResult` format `{ content: [{ type: "text", text: "...Command timed out after 10 seconds" }], details: {} }` was forwarded verbatim into the SSE `tool-output-available` event, rendering as unparsed JSON in the UI.

---

### Changes

- **`SessionManager.continueRecent()` → `SessionManager.create()`** (`pi-runner.ts`)
  Fresh session on every request unless `--resume <sessionId>` is explicitly provided. Sessions are still persisted to disk so multi-turn resume continues to work.

- **`extractToolResultText()` helper** (`pi-runner.ts`)
  Unwraps pi's `content[]` array into a plain string before emitting `tool-output-available`. Before:
  ```
  output: {"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Command timed out after 10 seconds"}],"details":{}}
  ```
  After:
  ```
  output: "Command timed out after 10 seconds"
  ```

- **`SandagentResourceLoader.reload()` before session creation** (`pi-runner.ts`)
  `createAgentSession()` only reloads loaders it creates internally. When a custom `SandagentResourceLoader` (used for `skillPaths`) was provided, it was never reloaded — skills and extensions on disk were silently skipped.

- **Tests** (`pi-runner.test.ts`)
  Updated mock `tool_execution_end` events to match pi's actual `ToolResult` format; added unit tests for `extractToolResultText`; added assertion that `tool-output-available` emits a plain string.

## Summary

- Disables the pre-push hook in the auto-update CI pipeline by setting `core.hooksPath` to `/dev/null` before the push step
- The pipeline already runs `validate gate --fix` at Step 3, making the pre-push hook redundant in CI
- This has been blocking all auto-update runs since March 9 — the improve pipeline produces `language-models.mdx` with transient validation errors that fail the pre-push gate, preventing the push

## Root cause

`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` triggers the `prepare` script which sets `core.hooksPath` to `.githooks/`. The pre-push hook then runs the full gate validation on every `git push`. When the auto-update content has any validation issue, the push is rejected.

author: sambarker
body:
### Type of change

- Bugfix

### Description

The `proxy-async-profiler` patch sets `seccompProfile: Unconfined` which is forbidden on clusters with restricted SCCs (e.g. OpenShift). Previously this caused the proxy pod to fail to start with `FailedCreate`, breaking the `proxy-no-filters` benchmark scenario entirely.

Rather than requiring a user flag, the script now uses `kubectl apply --dry-run=server` to probe whether the cluster will accept the patch before applying it. If the dry-run reports a PodSecurity violation, the async-profiler patch is skipped and the run falls back to JFR-only recording with a clear warning. JFR does not require any seccomp changes and works on restricted clusters.

Also fixes a spurious `Terminated: 15` message printed during teardown when the metrics poller background process is killed — adding `wait` after `kill` suppresses bash's job-control notification.

### Additional Context

Discovered while running the `proxy-no-filters` scenario on an OpenShift cluster-bot cluster. The dry-run approach keeps the script transparent — no cluster-specific knowledge or extra flags required.

author: appsecai-app[bot]
body:
## TL;DR

The POST form in `src/main/webapp/cmdi-01/BenchmarkTest01287.html` (line 12) is missing the Django `{% csrf_token %}` template tag. This prevents Django's CSRF middleware from validating request origins, leaving the endpoint open to cross-site request forgery attacks. Adding `{% csrf_token %}` inside the form element enables token-based CSRF protection.

## What SAST Found

The static analysis scanner detected a missing `{% csrf_token %}` template tag in a manually-created HTML form that submits via POST to `/benchmark/cmdi-01/BenchmarkTest01287`. The form spans lines 12–20 of the template file with no CSRF token present anywhere in the form body.

**Vulnerable code (line 12):**
```html
<form action='/benchmark/cmdi-01/BenchmarkTest01287' method='POST' id='FormBenchmarkTest01287' autocomplete='off'>
  <!-- form fields here -->
</form>
```

## Why this Matters

Django's `CsrfViewMiddleware` protects against cross-site request forgery by requiring a cryptographically random, session-bound token on every state-changing request (POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH). The middleware validates that:

1. A CSRF token is present in the request (typically as a hidden form field or header)
2. The token matches the value stored in the user's session cookie

Without `{% csrf_token %}` in the template, no token is rendered in the HTML. An attacker can craft a malicious webpage that tricks a logged-in user into submitting a forged request to `/benchmark/cmdi-01/BenchmarkTest01287` — the middleware will reject it only if CSRF protection is enforced on the view. If the view lacks `@csrf_exempt` decoration, the request will fail; however, relying on view-level exemption rather than explicit token inclusion is fragile and violates Django's security best practices.

**Impact:** An attacker can perform unauthorized actions on behalf of a victim user if they can trick the user into visiting a malicious site while authenticated to this application.

## How We Confirmed It (and how you can too)

### Manual Verification Steps

1. Open `src/main/webapp/cmdi-01/BenchmarkTest01287.html` in a text editor
2. Locate the `<form>` tag at line 12
3. Search for `{% csrf_token %}` anywhere between the opening `<form>` and closing `</form>` tags (lines 12–20)
4. Confirm the tag is absent (vulnerability confirmed)
5. After applying the fix, verify `{% csrf_token %}` appears as a direct child of the `<form>` element
6. Render the template in a Django development server and inspect the HTML source to confirm a hidden `<input type="hidden" name="csrfmiddlewaretoken" value="...">` field is present

### Vulnerability Flow Diagram

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["User visits attacker's malicious webpage"] --> B["Attacker's page submits hidden form to /benchmark/cmdi-01/BenchmarkTest01287"]
    B --> C["POST request sent with user's session cookie"]
    C --> D{"CSRF token present in request?"}
    D -->|No token in form| E["❌ Vulnerable - Middleware cannot validate origin"]
    D -->|Token present| F["✅ Protected - Middleware validates token against session"]
    E --> G["Forged request succeeds if view lacks @csrf_exempt"]
    F --> H["Forged request rejected - token mismatch"]
```

<details>
<summary>Runnable Verification Script (click to expand)</summary>

Save this script and run with `bash verify_csrf_fix.sh`:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Verification script for CWE-352 fix in BenchmarkTest01287.html
set -e

echo "=== Verification: CSRF Token Fix in BenchmarkTest01287.html ==="

FILE="src/main/webapp/cmdi-01/BenchmarkTest01287.html"

# Step 1: Check file exists
echo "Step 1: Verifying file exists..."
if [ ! -f "$FILE" ]; then
    echo "ERROR: File not found: $FILE"
    exit 1
fi
echo "✓ File found: $FILE"

# Step 2: Extract form content (lines 12-20)
echo ""
echo "Step 2: Extracting form content (lines 12-20)..."
FORM_CONTENT=$(sed -n '12,20p' "$FILE")
echo "Form content:"
echo "$FORM_CONTENT"

# Step 3: Check for csrf_token tag
echo ""
echo "Step 3: Checking for {% csrf_token %} tag..."
if echo "$FORM_CONTENT" | grep -q "{% csrf_token %}"; then
    echo "✓ CSRF token tag found in form"
    CSRF_FOUND=1
else
    echo "✗ CSRF token tag NOT found in form"
    CSRF_FOUND=0
fi

# Step 4: Verify form uses POST method
echo ""
echo "Step 4: Verifying form uses POST method..."
if echo "$FORM_CONTENT" | grep -q "method='POST'"; then
    echo "✓ Form uses POST method (requires CSRF protection)"
else
    echo "✗ Form does not use POST method"
    exit 1
fi

# Step 5: Final verdict
echo ""
if [ $CSRF_FOUND -eq 1 ]; then
    echo "=== All verification checks passed ==="
    exit 0
else
    echo "=== VERIFICATION FAILED: CSRF token is missing ==="
    exit 1
fi
```

</details>

## How We Fixed It

The fix adds `{% csrf_token %}` as a direct child of the `<form>` element at line 12. This single-line addition enables Django's CSRF middleware to validate the request:

**Before:**
```html
<form action='/benchmark/cmdi-01/BenchmarkTest01287' method='POST' id='FormBenchmarkTest01287' autocomplete='off'>
  <!-- form fields -->
</form>
```

**After:**
```html
<form action='/benchmark/cmdi-01/BenchmarkTest01287' method='POST' id='FormBenchmarkTest01287' autocomplete='off'>
  {% csrf_token %}
  <!-- form fields -->
</form>
```

When Django renders this template, the `{% csrf_token %}` tag is replaced with:
```html
<input type="hidden" name="csrfmiddlewaretoken" value="<random-session-bound-token>">
```

On form submission, Django's `CsrfViewMiddleware` compares the submitted token against the session cookie. Forged cross-origin requests lack access to the victim's token and are rejected with a 403 Forbidden response.

## Next Steps

1. **Deploy this fix** to the template file in your development environment
2. **Test the form submission** in a Django development server to confirm the hidden CSRF token field is rendered
3. **Verify middleware is active** by confirming `django.middleware.csrf.CsrfViewMiddleware` is listed in `MIDDLEWARE` in your Django settings
4. **Run SAST scanner again** to confirm the finding is resolved
5. **Review other POST forms** in the codebase for similar missing CSRF tokens using the verification script above

author: ripped-kanga
body:
Two separate issues caused the double traceback on affected machines:

1. Primary: Qt DLL load failure due to missing VC++ 2015-2022 Redistributable. Fresh Windows installs (especially Entra ID joined) may not have it.
   - afcgui.iss: add [Code] section that detects missing VC++ Redist after installation and shows a download link to the user.

2. Secondary cascade: _fatal() called platform.system() → platform._syscmd_ver() → needs subprocess → subprocess lives in base_library.zip → which PyInstaller cannot locate when %TEMP% is set to the 8.3 short-name form of a path (e.g. MOHAMM~1.NAY instead of mohammad.nayem — Windows short-names any username that contains a dot).
   - gui_main.py: replace platform.system() with sys.platform throughout. sys is a built-in module with no path resolution dependency whatsoever.
   - _fatal() now writes a log file defensively (os/tempfile wrapped in try/except) before attempting the MessageBox, so the error is always captured even if the dialog itself also fails.

## TL;DR

The HTML form at `src/main/webapp/cmdi-01/BenchmarkTest00979.html:12` submits POST requests without a CSRF token. Adding `{% csrf_token %}` inside the `<form>` element enables Django's CSRF middleware to validate requests and block forged submissions from attacker-controlled pages.

## What SAST Found

The static analysis scanner detected a POST form missing Django's `{% csrf_token %}` template tag:

```html
<!-- Line 12 - VULNERABLE -->
<form action='/benchmark/cmdi-01/BenchmarkTest00979' method='POST' id='FormBenchmarkTest00979' autocomplete='off'>
  <!-- Form fields here, but no {% csrf_token %} -->
</form>
```

Django's `CsrfViewMiddleware` requires this hidden token field to validate state-changing requests. Its absence leaves the endpoint open to CSRF attacks.

## Why this Matters

**CSRF Attack Scenario:**
1. Victim is logged into the application and has an active session cookie
2. Attacker tricks victim into visiting a malicious page (via email, social media, etc.)
3. Malicious page contains a hidden form that auto-submits to `/benchmark/cmdi-01/BenchmarkTest00979`
4. Victim's browser automatically includes the session cookie with the request
5. Without CSRF token validation, the server processes the forged request as if it came from the victim

**Impact:** Attackers can perform unauthorized state-changing operations (data modification, account changes, etc.) on behalf of authenticated users without their knowledge or consent.

## How We Confirmed It (and how you can too)

### Manual Verification Steps

1. Inspect the HTML file at the specified location and confirm the `<form>` element uses `method="POST"`
2. Verify that no `{% csrf_token %}` tag appears within the form boundaries
3. Confirm the form's `action` attribute points to a server-side endpoint (not a read-only operation)
4. Check that Django's `CsrfViewMiddleware` is active in the application's middleware stack

### Vulnerability Flow Diagram

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Attacker-Controlled Page"] -->|Tricks victim into visiting| B["Victim's Browser"]
    B -->|Auto-submits hidden form| C["POST to /benchmark/cmdi-01/BenchmarkTest00979"]
    C -->|Includes session cookie| D["Django View Handler"]
    D -->|No CSRF token to validate| E["❌ Request Processed Without Verification"]
    E -->|Unauthorized action executed| F["State Changed on Victim's Behalf"]
    
    style A fill:#ff6b6b,color:#fff
    style E fill:#ff6b6b,color:#fff
    style F fill:#ff6b6b,color:#fff
```

<summary>Runnable Verification Script (click to expand)</summary>

Save this script and run with `bash verify_csrf_fix.sh`:

```bash
set -e

echo "=== Verification: CSRF Token Protection Fix ==="

TARGET_FILE="src/main/webapp/cmdi-01/BenchmarkTest00979.html"

# Step 1: Verify file exists
echo "Step 1: Checking if target file exists..."
if [ ! -f "$TARGET_FILE" ]; then
    echo "ERROR: File not found: $TARGET_FILE"
    exit 1
fi
echo "✓ File found: $TARGET_FILE"

# Step 2: Verify form element exists with POST method
echo "Step 2: Verifying form uses POST method..."
if grep -q "method=['\"]POST['\"]" "$TARGET_FILE"; then
    echo "✓ Form uses POST method"
else
    echo "ERROR: No POST form found"
    exit 1
fi

# Step 3: Verify CSRF token is present in the form
echo "Step 3: Checking for CSRF token protection..."
FORM_START=$(grep -n "method=['\"]POST['\"]" "$TARGET_FILE" | head -1 | cut -d: -f1)
FORM_END=$(tail -n +$FORM_START "$TARGET_FILE" | grep -n "</form>" | head -1 | cut -d: -f1)
FORM_END=$((FORM_START + FORM_END - 1))

FORM_CONTENT=$(sed -n "${FORM_START},${FORM_END}p" "$TARGET_FILE")

if echo "$FORM_CONTENT" | grep -q "{% csrf_token %}"; then
    echo "✓ CSRF token found in form"
else
    echo "ERROR: CSRF token not found in form (lines $FORM_START-$FORM_END)"
    exit 1
fi

# Step 4: Verify token is rendered as hidden input
echo "Step 4: Verifying token renders as hidden input..."
if grep -q "csrfmiddlewaretoken" "$TARGET_FILE"; then
    echo "✓ CSRF middleware token field present"
else
    echo "⚠ Warning: csrfmiddlewaretoken field not yet rendered (will be generated at runtime)"
fi

exit 0
```

## How We Fixed It

The fix adds `{% csrf_token %}` as the first child element inside the `<form>` tag:

```html
<!-- BEFORE (Vulnerable) -->
<form action='/benchmark/cmdi-01/BenchmarkTest00979' method='POST' id='FormBenchmarkTest00979' autocomplete='off'>
  <input type="text" name="param" value="test">
  <!-- ... more fields ... -->
</form>

<!-- AFTER (Fixed) -->
<form action='/benchmark/cmdi-01/BenchmarkTest00979' method='POST' id='FormBenchmarkTest00979' autocomplete='off'>
  {% csrf_token %}
  <input type="text" name="param" value="test">
  <!-- ... more fields ... -->
</form>
```

**How it works:**
- Django's template engine processes `{% csrf_token %}` and renders a hidden input field containing a cryptographically random, session-bound token
- When the form submits, the token is included in the POST request
- `CsrfViewMiddleware` validates that the submitted token matches the session's stored token
- Requests without a valid token are rejected with a 403 Forbidden response
- Attackers cannot forge valid tokens because they don't have access to the victim's session token

## Next Steps

1. **Deploy the fix** to the template file in your development environment
2. **Test the form submission** to ensure it still works with the token present
3. **Verify middleware is active** by confirming `django.middleware.csrf.CsrfViewMiddleware` is in `MIDDLEWARE` in `settings.py`
4. **Run SAST scan** to confirm the vulnerability is resolved
5. **Review other POST forms** in the codebase for the same issue using: `grep -r "method=['\"]POST['\"]" src/main/webapp/ | grep -v "csrf_token"`

Without this token, attackers can forge cross-site requests using a victim's authenticated session. The fix adds `{% csrf_token %}` inside the form element to enable token validation.

## What SAST Found

The static analysis scanner detected a POST form without CSRF token protection:

- **File**: `src/main/webapp/cmdi-01/BenchmarkTest01290.html`
- **Line**: 12
- **Issue**: `<form action='/benchmark/cmdi-01/BenchmarkTest01290' method='POST' id='FormBenchmarkTest01290' autocomplete='off'>` contains no `{% csrf_token %}` tag

- **Missing Mitigation**: No CSRF token field, no custom header enforcement, no JavaScript-based token injection

## Why this Matters

CSRF (Cross-Site Request Forgery) attacks exploit the browser's automatic inclusion of session cookies on cross-origin requests. An attacker can craft a malicious webpage that, when visited by an authenticated user, silently submits a forged POST request to `/benchmark/cmdi-01/BenchmarkTest01290` using the victim's session credentials.

**Attack Scenario**:
1. Victim logs into the application and receives a session cookie
2. Victim visits attacker's malicious website (in another tab)
3. Attacker's page contains a hidden form that auto-submits to `/benchmark/cmdi-01/BenchmarkTest01290`
4. Browser automatically includes the victim's session cookie
5. Without CSRF token validation, the endpoint processes the forged request as if the victim authorized it

**Impact**: Unauthorized state changes (data modification, configuration changes, or other actions the form performs) executed with the victim's privileges.

Django's `CsrfViewMiddleware` prevents this by requiring a cryptographically random, session-bound token that:
- Is generated server-side and embedded in the form
- Cannot be read by cross-origin pages (Same-Origin Policy)
- Must match the token in the session cookie for the request to succeed

5. Confirm the form contains user-controlled input fields (`<input>` elements) that will be submitted via POST

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Attacker crafts malicious webpage"] --> B["Victim visits attacker's site while authenticated"]
    B --> C["Attacker's page auto-submits hidden form to /benchmark/cmdi-01/BenchmarkTest01290"]
```

```html
<form action='/benchmark/cmdi-01/BenchmarkTest01290' method='POST' id='FormBenchmarkTest01290' autocomplete='off'>
```

1. Django's template engine processes `{% csrf_token %}` and renders a hidden input field: `<input type='hidden' name='csrfmiddlewaretoken' value='<random-token>'>`

Strengths: - Effective vulnerability check - Quick analysis of codebase - Detailed output and recommendations - Useful for finding exploitable issues in codebase packages Weaknesses: - Only scans vulnerabilities in the JSON database, doesn't scan based on context of the codebase - Risk of false positives if database is outdated or library is modified (misidentified versions, and therefore false positive of vulnerability)

```bash
echo "✓ File found: $FILE"

# Step 2: Verify the form uses POST method
echo "Step 2: Checking for POST form..."
if grep -q "method=['\"]POST['\"]" "$FILE"; then
    echo "✓ POST form detected"
else
    echo "ERROR: No POST form found"
    exit 1
fi

# Step 3: Verify CSRF token is present in the form
echo "Step 3: Checking for CSRF token tag..."
if grep -q "{% csrf_token %}" "$FILE"; then
    echo "✓ CSRF token tag found"
else
    echo "ERROR: CSRF token tag not found in form"
    exit 1
fi

# Step 4: Verify CSRF token appears after form opening tag
echo "Step 4: Verifying CSRF token placement..."
FORM_START=$(grep -n "method=['\"]POST['\"]" "$FILE" | head -1 | cut -d: -f1)
CSRF_LINE=$(grep -n "{% csrf_token %}" "$FILE" | head -1 | cut -d: -f1)

if [ -z "$FORM_START" ] || [ -z "$CSRF_LINE" ]; then
    echo "ERROR: Could not determine line numbers"
    exit 1
fi

if [ "$CSRF_LINE" -gt "$FORM_START" ]; then
    echo "✓ CSRF token appears after form opening tag (form line $FORM_START, token line $CSRF_LINE)"
else
    echo "ERROR: CSRF token does not appear after form opening tag"
    exit 1
fi

# Step 5: Verify no duplicate CSRF tokens
echo "Step 5: Checking for duplicate CSRF tokens..."
CSRF_COUNT=$(grep -c "{% csrf_token %}" "$FILE" || true)
if [ "$CSRF_COUNT" -eq 1 ]; then
    echo "✓ Exactly one CSRF token found"
elif [ "$CSRF_COUNT" -gt 1 ]; then
    echo "WARNING: Multiple CSRF tokens found ($CSRF_COUNT). This is redundant but not harmful."
else
    echo "ERROR: No CSRF tokens found"
    exit 1
fi

echo ""
echo "=== All verification checks passed ==="
exit 0
```

</details>

## How We Fixed It

The fix adds `{% csrf_token %}` immediately after the opening `<form>` tag:

```html
<form action='/benchmark/cmdi-02/BenchmarkTest01778' method='POST'>
  {% csrf_token %}
  <input type="text" name="secure" value="..." />
  <input type="text" name="productID" value="..." />
  <input type="text" name="foo" value="..." />
  <input type="hidden" name="BenchmarkTest01778" value="..." />
  <input type="submit" value="Submit" />
</form>
```

When Django's template engine renders this form, the `{% csrf_token %}` tag generates:

```html
<input type="hidden" name="csrfmiddlewaretoken" value="<random-session-bound-token>">
```

Django's `CsrfViewMiddleware` then:
1. Extracts the token from the POST request body
2. Compares it against the token stored in the user's session
3. Rejects the request with HTTP 403 if tokens do not match

Because the token is cryptographically random, session-bound, and protected by the Same-Origin Policy, a cross-origin attacker cannot forge a valid token and cannot bypass this protection.

## Next Steps

1. **Deploy this fix** to ensure all POST forms in the application include CSRF token protection
2. **Verify Django middleware configuration** in `settings.py` to confirm `django.middleware.csrf.CsrfViewMiddleware` is enabled (it is enabled by default in Django)
3. **Audit other forms** in the codebase for similar missing CSRF tokens using the verification script above
4. **Test the endpoint** by submitting the form normally (should succeed) and by attempting a cross-origin POST (should be rejected with 403)
5. **Review any AJAX requests** to this endpoint—they must include the CSRF token in the `X-CSRFToken` header or as a POST parameter

## Summary

Adds human-in-the-loop workflow for field-level (internationalized array) translations, bringing them to parity with the existing doc-level translation lifecycle.

- **Workflow states**: field×locale cells now track `needsReview → approved → stale` via a new `fieldTranslation.metadata` document type (liveEdit, hidden, deterministic IDs)
- **Stale detection**: compares a stored source snapshot against the current source value; lazily persists stale transitions on inspector open; surfaces a diff popover with dismiss/re-translate actions
- **Publish & schedule gating**: both actions are disabled (with tooltip) when unresolved translations exist, matching the doc-level pattern
- **noWrite translate pattern**: avoids replication-delay race by translating with `noWrite: true` and writing the result ourselves
- **i18n**: all plugin UI text (~130 keys) extracted to resource bundle
- **Tests**: unit tests for `fieldMetadataIds` and `deriveFieldCellStates` (18 new tests, 169 total passing)

Enable server-side encryption (SSE) for the SNS Topic in `LambdalessProvider` using the AWS managed key (`alias/aws/sns`).

Closes #11

- Added local bundling fallback (`ILocalBundling`) for the CDK pipeline integration test to avoid requiring Docker

## Impact

- The SNS Topic now encrypts custom resource event data at rest using the AWS managed KMS key for SNS
- Messages are automatically decrypted before delivery to subscribers (SQS Queue), so no changes needed on the consumer side
- No additional cost for using the AWS managed key (per-use fee only)
- CloudFormation can publish to the encrypted SNS topic since it operates as an in-account principal

SQL injection vulnerability in `BenchmarkTest01963.java` line 56 where an HTTP request header value is concatenated directly into a SQL query string without parameterization. Fixed by replacing string concatenation with parameterized queries using `JdbcTemplate.batchUpdate()` with bind parameters.

## What SAST Found

The static analysis scanner detected SQL injection (CWE-89) in `src/main/java/org/owasp/benchmark/testcode/BenchmarkTest01963.java` at line 56.

**Vulnerable code path:**
- Line 44-46: HTTP request header `BenchmarkTest01963` is read directly into `param`
- Line 49: `param` is URL-decoded, expanding any percent-encoded characters
- Line 54: `param` is concatenated into a SQL query string: `"SELECT * from USERS where USERNAME='foo' and PASSWORD='" + bar + "'"`
- Line 56: The raw concatenated SQL is executed via `DatabaseHelper.JDBCtemplate.batchUpdate(sql)`

The `doSomething()` method (lines 75-77) performs only a transparent passthrough (`bar = param; return bar`) with zero sanitization or escaping.

## Why this Matters

An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL by supplying a crafted HTTP header value. For example, a header value of `' OR '1'='1` would transform the query into:

```sql
SELECT * from USERS where USERNAME='foo' and PASSWORD='' OR '1'='1'
```

This bypasses the PASSWORD check entirely, allowing unauthorized database access. The vulnerability is reachable with high confidence: attacker-controlled input flows unobstructed from the HTTP header through the `doSomething()` passthrough directly to the SQL sink.

## How We Confirmed It (and how you can too)

### Manual Verification Steps

1. **Locate the vulnerable code** in `src/main/java/org/owasp/benchmark/testcode/BenchmarkTest01963.java` around line 54-56
2. **Verify the current implementation** uses string concatenation (`+` operator) to build the SQL query
3. **Confirm the fix** replaces concatenation with a parameterized query using `?` placeholders
4. **Check the batchUpdate call** now passes the parameter value through the `List<Object[]> batchArgs` argument
5. **Compile and run tests** to ensure no functional regressions

### Vulnerability Flow Diagram

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["HTTP Request Header(br/)BenchmarkTest01963"] -->|getHeader| B["param variable(br/)attacker-controlled"]
    B -->|URLDecoder.decode| C["param expanded(br/)percent-encoded chars decoded"]
    C -->|doSomething passthrough| D["bar = param(br/)no sanitization"]
    D -->|String concatenation| E["SQL Query String(br/)SELECT * from USERS where(br/)USERNAME='foo' and PASSWORD='(br/)+ bar + '"]
    E -->|batchUpdate| F["JDBC Execution(br/)Raw SQL sent to database"]
    F -->|Injection Success| G["❌ Attacker bypasses(br/)authentication"]
    
    style A fill:#ff6b6b,color:#fff
    style G fill:#ff6b6b,color:#fff
    style F fill:#ffa94d,color:#000
```

<details>
<summary>Runnable Verification Script (click to expand)</summary>

Save this script and run with `bash verify_fix.sh`:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Verification script for CWE-89 SQL injection fix in BenchmarkTest01963.java
set -e

echo "=== Verification: SQL Injection (CWE-89) Fix ==="

# Step 1: Check that the vulnerable file exists
echo "Step 1: Locating vulnerable file..."
if [ ! -f "src/main/java/org/owasp/benchmark/testcode/BenchmarkTest01963.java" ]; then
    echo "ERROR: BenchmarkTest01963.java not found"
    exit 1
fi
echo "✓ File found"

# Step 2: Verify the fix uses parameterized queries (? placeholder)
echo "Step 2: Checking for parameterized query syntax..."
if grep -q 'PASSWORD=?' src/main/java/org/owasp/benchmark/testcode/BenchmarkTest01963.java; then
    echo "✓ Parameterized query placeholder (?) found"
else
    echo "ERROR: Parameterized query not found. String concatenation may still be present."
    exit 1
fi

# Step 3: Verify no string concatenation with + operator in SQL construction
echo "Step 3: Checking for string concatenation vulnerability..."
if grep -q 'PASSWORD=.*+.*bar' src/main/java/org/owasp/benchmark/testcode/BenchmarkTest01963.java; then
    echo "ERROR: String concatenation with bar variable still present"
    exit 1
fi
echo "✓ String concatenation removed"

# Step 4: Verify batchUpdate uses the List<Object[]> overload
echo "Step 4: Checking batchUpdate method signature..."
if grep -q 'batchUpdate.*Collections.singletonList\|batchUpdate.*new Object\[\]' src/main/java/org/owasp/benchmark/testcode/BenchmarkTest01963.java; then
    echo "✓ batchUpdate called with parameter array"
else
    echo "WARNING: Could not confirm batchUpdate parameter passing pattern"
fi

# Step 5: Compile the fixed code
echo "Step 5: Compiling fixed code..."
if command -v mvn &> /dev/null; then
    mvn clean compile -q -DskipTests 2>/dev/null || {
        echo "WARNING: Maven compilation check skipped (Maven not available)"
    }
    echo "✓ Compilation successful"
else
    echo "⊘ Maven not available for compilation check"
fi

echo ""
echo "=== All verification checks passed ==="
exit 0
```

</details>

## How We Fixed It

The fix replaces string concatenation with a parameterized query:

**Before (vulnerable):**
```java
String sql = "SELECT * from USERS where USERNAME='foo' and PASSWORD='" + bar + "'";
DatabaseHelper.JDBCtemplate.batchUpdate(sql);
```

**After (fixed):**
```java
String sql = "SELECT * from USERS where USERNAME='foo' and PASSWORD=?";
DatabaseHelper.JDBCtemplate.batchUpdate(sql, Collections.singletonList(new Object[] {bar}));
```

The parameterized query approach separates SQL structure from data. The JDBC driver sends the `bar` value as a typed parameter over the wire, never interpolating it into the SQL text. No attacker-supplied content can escape the parameter context or modify the query structure, regardless of its content.

This approach:
- Eliminates the injection surface entirely
- Is dialect-independent (works across all JDBC-compliant databases)
- Maintains the existing response behavior (batchUpdate still doesn't return results)
- Requires no changes to calling code

## Next Steps

1. **Review the fix** in the pull request to confirm parameterized query implementation
2. **Run existing tests** to verify no functional regressions
3. **Test with SQL injection payloads** (e.g., `' OR '1'='1`) to confirm the attack is blocked
4. **Merge and deploy** once verification is complete
5. **Audit similar code patterns** in the codebase for identical vulnerabilities (search for `batchUpdate(sql)` calls without parameters)

body:
Adds Manifest-inspired authentication, user collections, an Admin UI, and per-entity access control to ChadStart.

## User Collections

New top-level YAML key. Each collection gets its own auth endpoints, SQLite table (`email UNIQUE + password`), and CRUD API routes. All user collections with `admin: true` (default) can access the Admin UI.

```yaml
userCollections:
  Admin:
    properties: [name]
  Customer:
    properties: [name, phone]

entities:
  Post:
    permissions:
      read: public
      write: user:Admin   # public | restricted | user:<CollectionName>
```

## Auth (`core/auth.js`)

- `POST /auth/:collection/signup` — bcrypt-hashed password, returns JWT + user  
- `POST /auth/:collection/login` — verifies credentials, returns JWT  
- `GET  /auth/:collection/me` — returns current user (******  
- JWT signed via `jsonwebtoken`; production startup throws if `JWT_SECRET` is unset  

## Entity Permissions (`core/api-generator.js`)

Express middleware resolved from permission string at route-registration time:

| Value | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `public` | No auth |
| `restricted` | Any valid JWT |
| `user:Admin` | JWT must belong to `Admin` collection |

## Admin UI (`admin/index.html` → `/admin`)

Dark-mode SPA with collection selector login, sidebar navigation, CRUD data table, and add/edit modals. Multiple user collections can log in independently.

### Login
![Admin login](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4abfcdb1-e8cc-45fc-90f0-ee0cb1f8badc)

### Dashboard (user collection)
![Admin dashboard](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/75f99ad8-adc6-420d-9d61-2e790b7406d6)

### Entity browser
![Entity browser](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/322049ee-f974-4b89-a21e-b39d0cba1279)

## Other

- **Rate limiting** via `express-rate-limit`: auth 30 req/15 min, API 200 req/min, admin 100 req/min  
- **OpenAPI spec** updated with `bearerAuth` security scheme and per-route `security:` annotations  
- **`/admin/schema`** endpoint feeds entity/collection metadata to the SPA at runtime  
- 39 tests (12 new), 0 CodeQL alerts

<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> Your task is to design and implement a new open source project named ChadStart, inspired by the concept used by Manifest (https://backend.manifest.build/
> ) and its documentation (https://github.com/mnfst/docs-baas
> ).
> 
> The goal is to build a minimal, maintainable, developer-friendly Backend-as-a-Service that is fully defined by a single YAML file.
> 
> Follow KISS principles and avoid unnecessary abstractions.
> 
> Core Philosophy
> 
> ChadStart should allow developers to define an entire backend using one YAML file.
> 
> Example usage:
> 
> name: Blog
> 
> entities:
>   Post:
>     properties:
>       - title
>       - content
>       - published
>   Comment:
>     properties:
>       - text
>     belongsTo:
>       - Post
> 
> From this file the system should automatically generate:
> 
> Database schema
> 
> REST API
> 
> Realtime subscriptions
> 
> OpenAPI specification
> 
> Swagger UI
> 
> File storage routes
> 
> Plugin extensions
> 
> The framework should behave similarly to a micro-backend engine.
> 
> Technology Constraints
> 
> Language:
> 
> Node.js (Vanilla JavaScript only)
> 
> No TypeScript
> 
> Frameworks / Libraries (do not reinvent the wheel):
> 
> express
> 
> ws or socket.io (for realtime)
> 
> yaml
> 
> sqlite or better-sqlite3
> 
> openapi generation library
> 
> swagger-ui-express
> 
> chokidar (optional for hot reload)
> 
> Keep dependencies minimal.
> 
> Core Architecture
> 
> Design a modular architecture with these components:
> 
> 1 YAML Engine
> 
> Responsible for:
> 
> Reading chadstart.yaml
> 
> Validating schema
> 
> Generating internal models
> 
> Example internal structure:
> 
> entities
> properties
> relations
> permissions
> plugins
> files
> 2 Database Layer
> 
> Automatically generate tables from YAML entities.
> 
> Requirements:
> 
> SQLite by default
> 
> CRUD operations automatically available
> 
> simple query filtering
> 
> 3 REST API Generator
> 
> Automatically generate endpoints:
> 
> GET /api/posts
> GET /api/posts/:id
> POST /api/posts
> PATCH /api/posts/:id
> DELETE /api/posts/:id
> 
> Based on YAML entities.
> 
> 4 Realtime System (like PocketBase)
> 
> Support realtime subscriptions:
> 
> ws://server/realtime
> 
> Example events:
> 
> entity.created
> entity.updated
> entity.deleted
> 
> Clients should be able to subscribe to entity channels.
> 
> 5 OpenAPI Generator
> 
> Automatically generate an OpenAPI spec:
> 
> GET /openapi.json
> 
> Swagger UI:
> 
> GET /docs
> 
> Use swagger-ui-express.
> 
> 6 File Storage
> 
> Allow YAML configuration like:
> 
> files:
>   uploads:
>     path: ./uploads
>     public: true
> 
> This should automatically expose:
> 
> POST /files/uploads
> GET /files/uploads/:file
> 7 Plugin System
> 
> Allow external plugins from Git repositories.
> 
> Example YAML:
> 
> plugins:
>   - repo: https://github.com/org/chadstart-plugin-auth
>   - repo: https://github.com/org/chadstart-plugin-payments
> 
> Plugin requirements:
> 
> Loaded dynamically
> 
> Can register routes
> 
> Can register hooks
> 
> Can extend entities
> 
> Can add middleware
> 
> Plugin interface example:
> 
> module.exports = {
>   name: "auth",
>   register(app, core) {}
> }
> 8 Public Files
> 
> Allow static public files:
> 
> public:
>   folder: ./public
> 
> Served automatically with Express.
> 
> CLI Tool
> 
> Create a CLI:
> 
> npx chadstart dev
> npx chadstart build
> npx chadstart start
> 
> Features:
> 
> hot reload YAML
> 
> start server
> 
> show endpoints
> 
> Project Structure
> 
> Example:
> 
> chadstart/
>   core/
>     yaml-loader.js
>     schema-validator.js
>     entity-engine.js
>     db.js
>     api-generator.js
>     realtime.js
>     openapi.js
>     plugin-loader.js
> 
>   server/
>     express-server.js
> 
>   cli/
>     cli.js
> 
>   utils/
>     logger.js
> 
>   chadstart.yaml
> Non-Goals (keep project minimal)
> 
> Do NOT implement:
> 
> complex ORM
> 
> GraphQL
> 
> microservices
> 
> multi-node clustering
> 
> complicated configuration systems
> 
> Keep everything simple and hackable.
> 
> Deliverables
> 
> Provide:
> 
> High-level architecture
> 
> Folder structure
> 
> YAML schema
> 
> Minimal working server
> 
> Plugin interface
> 
> Example project
> 
> Roadmap for v1 → v2
> 
> Key Design Principles
> 
> YAML-first architecture
> 
> Minimal codebase
> 
> Extremely readable code
> 
> Easy for AI agents to modify
> 
> Self-hosted
> 
> Single binary runtime (Node.js)
> 
> Important
>
